properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 25 at 10:30PM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
At 1030 PM MDT/1130 PM CDT/, Doppler radar was tracking a strong
thunderstorm 16 miles southeast of Tribune, moving east at 5 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 55 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of southwestern
Wichita and southeastern Greeley Counties.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 25 at 11:29PM CDT by NWS La Crosse WI
properties.description:

a line extending from near Humbird to 8 miles southwest of Alma
Center to near Arcadia. Movement was southeast at 25 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Merrillan and Alma Center around 1135 PM CDT.

Hatfield around 1145 PM CDT.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 25 at 11:47PM EDT until August 26 at 2:45AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Decatur County in southwestern Georgia...

* Until 245 AM EDT.

* At 1147 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Brinson, Decatur Co A/P, Cyrene, Ausmac, Hanover and Eldorendo.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

at 1:30 PM EDT /12:30 PM CDT/ Tuesday was 17.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 18.0 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
Thursday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 1000 AM CDT
/1100 AM EDT/.
